passage: Managing personal finances effectively requires a clear understanding of how money functions. A budget is a flexible plan that allocates your income toward essential needs, such as food and education, before considering wants like luxury items. Many people mistakenly believe that savings are simply what remains after spending, but true financial security comes from saving a portion of your income first. When you deposit money into a bank, it does not sit in a private box; instead, the bank uses those funds to provide loans, and in return, they pay you interest. This interest causes your savings to grow over time even if you do not add more money, as the bank calculates earnings on your existing balance. Unlike a piggy bank, which keeps money stagnant, a bank account helps your wealth increase through compound interest. Furthermore, savings are not just for purchasing desired goods; they are a vital safety net for emergencies like medical expenses or unexpected job loss. By prioritizing savings and understanding that a budget must adapt to changing circumstances, you can build a stable financial future. Remember that income can come from various sources beyond a formal salary, and distinguishing between essential needs and temporary desires is the first step toward responsible money management.

items.evidence: Many people mistakenly believe that savings are simply what remains after spending, but true financial security comes from saving a portion of your income first.
items.q: Meera spends her pocket money freely and saves what remains. What should she do instead?
options: Save a part of it first, then spend
Keep saving whatever is left after spending
Save only once she has a large amount
Save only when she wants to buy something
items.explain: True security comes from saving a part of income first, not from saving what remains.

wrong.why: thinks savings are just the leftover after spending
thinks saving is useless unless the amount is big
thinks savings are only for buying wanted things

items.evidence: When you deposit money into a bank, it does not sit in a private box; instead, the bank uses those funds to provide loans, and in return, they pay you interest.
items.q: Why does a bank pay interest to people who deposit money?
options: Because it lends that money to other people
Because it keeps your notes in a box
Because interest is a free gift from it
Because you borrow loans from the bank
items.explain: The bank lends deposited money as loans and pays you interest in return.

wrong.why: thinks the bank stores actual notes in a box
thinks interest is a gift with no reason
mixes up the depositor with the borrower

items.evidence: This interest causes your savings to grow over time even if you do not add more money, as the bank calculates earnings on your existing balance.
items.q: Sunil deposits Rs 1,000 in a bank once and adds nothing. What happens to his balance over years?
options: It grows, as interest is earned on it
It stays Rs 1,000 until he adds more
It grows only if he adds money monthly
It falls because the bank lends it out
items.explain: Interest is earned on the existing balance, so savings grow even without adding more money.

wrong.why: thinks a bank account keeps money stagnant like a piggy bank
thinks growth needs new deposits every time
thinks lending the money makes the balance shrink

items.evidence: Furthermore, savings are not just for purchasing desired goods; they are a vital safety net for emergencies like medical expenses or unexpected job loss.
items.q: Kiran's father suddenly loses his job. How could the family's savings help?
options: They would pay for needs until he works again
They could be used only for buying wants
They would be useless unless the sum is big
They would be spent first on luxury items
items.explain: Savings are a safety net for emergencies like unexpected job loss, not only for buying wants.

wrong.why: thinks savings are never for emergencies
thinks wants should be bought first

items.evidence: By prioritizing savings and understanding that a budget must adapt to changing circumstances, you can build a stable financial future.
items.q: Ria's family made a budget last year, but rent has now gone up. What should they do?
options: Change it to fit the new costs
Keep it the same, as budgets are fixed
Drop it, since income will cover everything
Put wants first to stay happy
items.explain: A budget is flexible and must adapt to changing circumstances.

wrong.why: thinks a budget should never be changed
thinks enough income removes the need for choices
thinks wants should come first because they please us
